{{Jargon|date=September 2024}}

In [[semigroup theory]], a '''Schützenberger group''' is a [[group (mathematics)|group]] associated with a [[Green's relations#The H and D relations|Green {{nowrap|''H''-class}}]] of a [[semigroup]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://scholarsmine.mst.edu/comsci_facwork/388/ |title=The Schützenberger Group of an H-class in the Semigroup of Binary Relations by Robert L. Brandon, Darel W. Hardy, George Markowsky, Missouri University of Science and Technology, 1972-12-01|journal=Semigroup Forum |date=December 1972 |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=45–53 |doi=10.1007/BF02572873 |last1=Brandon |first1=Robert |last2=Hardy |first2=Darel |last3=Markowsky |first3=George |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The Schützenberger groups associated with different {{nowrap|''H''-classes}} are distinct, but the groups associated with two different {{nowrap|''H''-classes}} contained in the same {{nowrap|''D''-class}} of a semigroup are [[isomorphic]]. Moreover, if the {{nowrap|''H''-class}} itself were a group, the Schützenberger group of the {{nowrap|''H''-class}} would be isomorphic to the {{nowrap|''H''-class}}. In fact, there are two Schützenberger groups associated with a given {{nowrap|''H''-class}}, with each being [[antiisomorphism|antiisomorphic]] to the other.

The Schützenberger group was discovered by [[Marcel-Paul Schützenberger]] in 1957<ref>{{cite journal|last=Marcel-Paul Schützenberger|year=1957|title=D-representation des demi-groupes|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|volume=244|pages=1994&ndash;1996}} (MR 19, 249)</ref><ref>{{Cite book | last1=Clifford | first1=Alfred Hoblitzelle | author1-link=Alfred H. Clifford | last2=Preston | first2=Gordon Bamford | author2-link=Gordon Preston | title=The algebraic theory of semigroups. Vol. I | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | location=Providence, R.I. | series=Mathematical Surveys, No. 7 | isbn=978-0-8218-0272-4 |mr=0132791 | year=1961 }} (pp.&nbsp;63&ndash;66)</ref>, and the terminology was coined by [[A. H. Clifford]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v3i1f1/html|title=Marcel-Paul Schützenberger (1920&ndash;1996)|last=Wilf|first=Herbert |date=August 29, 1996|journal=The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics|volume=3 |doi=10.37236/2063 |accessdate=2015-12-30|display-authors=etal|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==The Schützenberger group==
Let ''S'' be a semigroup and let ''S''<sup>1</sup> be the semigroup obtained by adjoining an [[identity element]] 1 to ''S'' (if ''S'' already has an identity element, then ''S''<sup>1</sup> = ''S''). Green's {{nowrap|''H''-relation}} in ''S'' is defined as follows: If ''a'' and ''b'' are in ''S'' then

:''a'' ''H'' ''b''  ⇔ there are ''u'', ''v'', ''x'', ''y'' in ''S''<sup>1</sup>  such that ''ua'' = ''ax'' = ''b'' and ''vb'' = ''by'' = ''a''.

For ''a'' in ''S'', the set of all ''b'''&thinsp;s in ''S'' such that ''a'' ''H'' ''b'' is the Green {{nowrap|''H''-class}} of ''S'' containing ''a'', denoted by ''H''<sub>''a''</sub>.

Let ''H'' be an {{nowrap|''H''-class}} of the semigroup ''S''.  Let ''T''(''H'') be the set of all elements ''t'' in ''S''<sup>1</sup> such that ''Ht'' is a subset of ''H'' itself. Each ''t'' in ''T''(''H'') defines a transformation, denoted by γ<sub>''t''</sub>, of ''H'' by mapping ''h'' in ''H'' to ''ht'' in ''H''.  The set of all these transformations of ''H'', denoted by Γ(''H''), is a group under [[function composition|composition]] of mappings (taking functions as right operators). The group Γ(''H'') is the Schützenberger group associated with the {{nowrap|''H''-class}} ''H''.

== Examples ==
{{Expand section|date=June 2009}}

If ''H'' is a maximal subgroup of a [[monoid]] ''M'', then ''H'' is an {{nowrap|H-class}}, and it is naturally isomorphic to its own Schützenberger group.

In general, one has that the [[cardinality]] of ''H'' and its Schützenberger group coincide for any {{nowrap|H-class}} ''H''.

== Applications ==
{{Expand section|date=June 2009}}

It is known that a monoid with finitely many left and right [[Semigroup#Subsemigroups and ideals|ideals]] is [[finitely presented monoid|finitely presented]] (or just [[finitely generated monoid|finitely generated]]) [[if and only if]] all of its Schützenberger groups are [[finitely presented group|finitely presented]] (respectively, [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]]).<!-- Ruskuc 2000 according to http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/~robertg/RGray_ApproachingCosets.pdf -->  Similarly such a monoid is [[residually finite]] if and only if all of its Schützenberger groups are residually finite.<!-- Gray and Ruskuc 2007 according to same source -->
